entities.name: great pollard willow with a forked top (隋堤烟柳, west of the three)
entities.what: Huge old pollard willow (willow_burl): a thick burled bole about 130 px wide at the foot, pale-barked between dark lumpy contours, leaning west as it rises; at about v 1100 it forks into two short limbs, each ending in a knobbly clubbed pollard head (west head about (32275, 1040), east head about (32345, 1015)), from which fans of long straight bare whips rise and spread west over the open ground. Early spring: bare, at most a faint haze. Stands just behind (north of) the great willow S1.tree.willow_burl_great_32620.
entities.vis: part: the crown's upper whips merge with the whips of S1.tree.willow_burl_great_32620 and of t3's great willow (base about 32030)
entities.src: 余辉: 隋堤烟柳; 名画记: 隋堤烟柳 (pin 3)
entities.note: Foot = where the trunk's lower end meets the pale ground at v 1420-1440, u 32400-32480 (zoom 2.4-3, raised contrast); B's left contour runs down-right beside it, so the two boles touch here but their feet are about 155 px apart in v; the restyle draws the foot about 25 px lower (v 1460): not used. Trunk 32330-32445 at v 1300, 32258-32391 at v 1100. The two dark bands of the trunk with a pale stripe between are read as one bole's contours (pale bark), not two stems; the restyle paints two stems merging at the foot: if two, they share this foot. Crown points are est: A's whips can be told from B's only near the heads; the high fans at v 290-530 over 32265-32600 are given to B. Painted height to the head ≈ 420 px (1437 -> 1015), to the est crown top ≈ 990 px.

entities.name: the greatest of the old pollard willows (隋堤烟柳, middle)
entities.what: The largest tree of the countryside: a massive, dark, lumpy and moss-dotted bole 150-200 px wide with exposed knobbly roots running east along the ground to about u 32845; the bole leans west as it rises to a broad knobbly pollard head of two or three clubbed knobs (u 32400-32600, v 930-1055), from which a fountain of long straight bare whips rises to the top of the crown (v ≈ 290) and spreads from about 32230 to 32790. Early spring: bare, the whip tips drawn in fine pale fans.
entities.vis: part: whips overlap the crowns of S1.tree.willow_burl_forked_32448 and S1.tree.willow_burl_leaning_east_32805, and hide the feet of the far trees behind
entities.src: 余辉: 隋堤烟柳; 名画记: 隋堤烟柳 (pin 3)
entities.note: Foot: the trunk meets the ground at v 1580-1592 between about u 32540 and 32706 (zoom 2.4-3); the root flare continues east as a band of dark knobs at 32700-32845, v 1540-1605, read as this tree's exposed roots (the restyle splits it into a root and a separate rock outcrop with grass; if it is a rock it is structures_w's ground). Trunk spans 32460-32620 at v 1200 and 32460-32670 at v 1300. The dark knots on the bole (32480-32620, v 1170-1370) are burls/moss dots; the restyle turns them into ivy leaves: no ivy is painted. Crown attribution: the high fine fans at v 290-530 (u 32265-32600) and v 465-650 (u 32530-32800) are read as this tree's whip tips (no other head or trunk is painted under them); they could hide far willow heads, but none shows. Painted height ≈ 1300 px (1588 -> 290). SCALE CUE: bole about 150 px wide at v 1500. SECOND PASS (willows), the flagged 'roots or a rock': the knobbly mass east of B's foot is a low lobe from u 32723 to 32860. Its base line runs along v 1585-1595, continuous with B's foot line, and it has two bumps, a peak at (32775, 1543) and a second at (32815-32827, 1545-1550). It has a pale lit face on its west part (32750-32773, 1553-1583) and dense dark knobs and dots on its east part. Between the trunk's own flare (it sweeps down into the ground at about 32705-32740, v 1582-1600) and the lobe there is only a narrow pale gap above v 1585. Kept as B's exposed roots. The burled willow S1.tree.willow_great_burl_32065 has its root lobes drawn in the same way (pale-topped lobes with dark knobbed edges at 32057-32128, v 1455-1500 and 32152-32286, v 1400-1500), and the map already reads those as roots. Read both alike. If the lead reads them as rocks, all three lobes become grd rocks together, with base corners from the extents given here.

entities.name: great pollard willow leaning east (隋堤烟柳, east of the three)
entities.what: Huge old pollard willow (willow_burl): a lumpy, dark-knotted bole with a root flare to the west, leaning east as it rises from the foot to a fork at about (32930, 1100); a west limb ends in a knobbly head at (32825-32900, v 1000-1080) and an east limb in heads at (32940-33085, v 978-1060); long bare whips rise to v ≈ 630 and sweep east as far as u ≈ 33410, their ends drooping to v 1050-1110. Early spring: bare. The easternmost of the great willows; open ink-wash ground lies east of it.
entities.src: 余辉: 隋堤烟柳; 名画记: 隋堤烟柳 (pin 3)
entities.note: Foot at v 1383-1400 between u 32734 and 32884 (root flare at the west end, 32734-32773); trunk 32762-32879 at v 1339, 32829-32951 at v 1200, 32873-32996 at v 1100. Crown_w est: the west whips mingle with B's crown at 32650-32750. Crown_e: the whips reach 33400-33433 at v 800-870 (u > 33200, but by its base the tree is t4's). Painted height ≈ 765 px (1395 -> 630). DEPTH: its foot (v 1395) is about 190 px up the silk from B's (v 1588), so it stands well behind B. MERGE: t5's "low pollard willow, stubby gnarled bole at 33010-33095, v 990-1052, base about (33055, 1050)" with shoots fanning north-east over 33100-33420 is this tree's east head (heads at 32940-33085, v 978-1060), not another tree (merge crop at zoom 1 over 32850-33550).

entities.name: far bare tree at the top, behind the great willows
entities.what: Far bare tree (elm_claw, small and faint) seen above the great willows' crowns: a straight trunk carrying a spreading crown of twisted, angular, crab-claw branches with no leaves.
entities.vis: part: trunk below v ≈ 330 hidden by the whips of S1.tree.willow_burl_great_32620
entities.note: Trunk 32486-32518 visible from v 210 to about 330 (raised-contrast crop). Base est at v 655, the foot line where three trunks of the same far grove end (S1.tree.far_bare_elm_32932, _33009, _33061 at v 640-657); its true foot is hidden and could be higher up the silk (a smaller, nearer-the-horizon tree). The restyle turns it into a green weeping willow and adds a walking man at (32430, 175-260): the scan has only faint branches there.

entities.name: far bare tree with a leaning trunk
entities.what: Far bare tree (elm_claw, small and faint): a thin trunk leaning west as it falls, under a flat crown of twisted horizontal branches with knotty twig clusters, no leaves.
entities.vis: part: trunk below v ≈ 450 hidden by the great willows' whips
entities.note: Trunk visible from (32682, 243) to (32654, 449), sloping du/dv ≈ -0.14; base est by extending that line to the grove's foot line v 655. The crown (32645-32800, v 199-300) could instead belong to S1.tree.far_slender_32753, whose fork reaches up to its dark junction at (32705, 292); the restyle gives the crown to this leaning trunk and paints it as a weeping willow (no hanging strands on the scan).

entities.name: faint far sapling
entities.what: Very faint thin bare sapling (slender form) in the far grove, a single stem with a small fork at the top.
entities.note: Stem 32712-32720 from v 395 to 472 (raised contrast, zoom 2.6-3.5), forking at v 395-420; below v 472 the willow whips hide it. Could be a branch of S1.tree.far_bare_leaning_32628 or of _32753 rather than its own tree.

entities.name: far slender bare tree
entities.what: Far slender bare tree: a thin straight trunk forking near the top into a few bare branches.
entities.vis: part: trunk below v ≈ 500 hidden by the great willows' whips
entities.note: Trunk 32746-32758 visible v 341-501, nearly vertical; fork at v 330-370, one branch up-left to the dark junction at (32705, 292). Base est on the grove's foot line (v 655).

entities.name: far slender bare tree (two stems)
entities.what: Far slender bare tree: a thin trunk with a second, thinner stem beside it, both rising to small forks of bare twigs.
entities.vis: part: stems below v ≈ 490 hidden by the great willows' whips
entities.note: Main stem 32771-32780 visible v 355-490, slanting slightly east as it falls; a thinner stem at 32789-32794 (v 396-484) runs beside it and is read as a second stem of the same tree (they converge toward the hidden foot). Base est by extending the stem to v 655.

entities.name: far twin-stemmed bare tree
entities.what: Far bare tree of two thin stems from one (hidden) foot, each forking at the top into upright bare twigs (slender form).
entities.vis: part: stems below v ≈ 553 hidden by the great willows' whips
entities.note: West stem 32803 (v 423) -> 32820 (v 550), slanting east as it falls; east stem 32833 (v 440) -> 32838 (v 550), near vertical; extended, they meet at about v 650-700, so one tree with two stems (the restyle also draws one forked tree here). If the stems are two trees, the second foot is about 15 px west.

entities.name: far slender bare tree
entities.what: Far slender bare tree: a thin straight trunk with a spray of upright forking bare branches at the top.
entities.vis: part: trunk below v ≈ 557 hidden by the great willows' whips
entities.note: Trunk 32857-32871 visible v 407-557, near vertical; branches 32830-32900, v 359-444. Base est on the grove's foot line.

entities.name: small far bare tree
entities.what: Small far bare tree (elm_claw, small): a short dark trunk with angular crab-claw branches spreading west and east, and one long thin branch rising to the north-west.
entities.vis: part: foot hidden by the whip tips of S1.tree.willow_burl_leaning_east_32805
entities.note: Trunk 32921-32938 visible v 540-657 and thickening at the bottom; branches 32895-32997 at v 516-594. The thin stem at 32884-32897 (v 366-535) is read as this tree's long north-west branch (it meets the crown at about (32920, 560)); it could be a separate sapling. Base est just below the last trunk stroke.

entities.name: far bare tree
entities.what: Far bare tree (elm_claw): a straight dark trunk rising to angular crab-claw branches with knobbly twig clusters, no leaves.
entities.vis: part: foot hidden by the whip tips of S1.tree.willow_burl_leaning_east_32805
entities.note: Trunk 33002-33021 visible v 502-640, darker and thicker at v 598-635 (near its foot). Branches cross those of S1.tree.far_bare_elm_33061 at 33030-33050.

entities.name: far bare tree forking in two
entities.what: Far bare tree (elm_claw): a straight trunk forking at about v 470 into two limbs, west and north-east, ending in angular crab-claw twigs, no leaves.
entities.vis: part: foot hidden by the whip tips of S1.tree.willow_burl_leaning_east_32805
entities.note: Trunk 33052-33071 visible v 478-648; fork at v 470-480; north-east limb to (33121, 378), twigs to 33150. The far grove's foot line (v 640-660) is set by this tree, S1.tree.far_bare_elm_33009 and S1.tree.far_bare_elm_32932.

entities.name: thin stalk or stake on the open ground
entities.what: A single thin dotted ink stroke standing on the pale open ground south-east of the east great willow's foot: read as one tall reed or grass stalk, or a thin stake stuck in the ground.
entities.note: Dotted line 2-3 px wide from (32866, 1486) to (32882, 1541), 55 px long, leaning north-west (zoom 5). Both readings: a reed/grass stalk (then ground texture, droppable) or a small stake (a prop). The restyle copies it as a dashed line. It is not a silk crack (the dots are ink).
